title: Finalize marketplace SKU taxonomy + naming conventions (Hosted/Dedicated/Private + add-ons) and map to internal plans
creator: Nikhil Sharma
description:
Context
- We need consistent SKU names and taxonomy across AWS Marketplace + GCP Marketplace + Redwood Console + internal billing/entitlements.
- Goal is enterprise procurement-friendly packaging without breaking developer-first onboarding.
- This ticket finalizes: (1) SKU families, (2) naming conventions, (3) add-on structure, and (4) mapping to internal plan codes / entitlement IDs.

Links
- Confluence PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/cloud-marketplace-listing-refresh-prd.json
- Packaging proposal v2: sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/marketplace-sku-catalog-and-packaging-v2.json
- ADR (naming + entitlement IDs): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-marketplace-sku-naming-and-entitlement-ids.json
- Mapping sheet (working): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/marketplace-sku-mapping-sheet.json

Decision summary (final)
1) SKU families (top-level taxonomy)
- Hosted API: usage-based (metered) marketplace offer(s)
- Dedicated Capacity: contract-based reserved capacity (by capacity tier; metering handled within Redwood)
- Private Deployment: contract-based platform license (VPC; on-prem available via Private, not a separate marketplace listing where constrained)
- Add-ons: separate line items where marketplace supports it; otherwise bundled into higher-tier SKUs (documented per marketplace).

2) Naming convention (canonical names used in copy + console + quoting)
- Format: "Redwood Inference — <Product> — <Plan/Tier> [— <Region/Term> if required by marketplace]"
- Rules:
  - Use em dash separators (—) in canonical naming; fall back to hyphens only if marketplace field restrictions require.
  - No vendor-specific terms in the SKU name (avoid "AWS", "GCP"); marketplace listing page already scopes environment.
  - Avoid ambiguous infra terms like "endpoint" or "cluster" in the SKU name; reserve for description.
  - Use "Hosted API" / "Dedicated Capacity" / "Private Deployment" as the product surface area labels.
  - Add-ons must start with "Add-on" to reduce confusion in procurement systems.

3) Tiering
- Hosted API tiers:
  - Starter (self-serve / low-commit)
  - Business (committed spend)
  - Enterprise (committed spend + enterprise controls available)
  Note: Hosted tiers are primarily commercial packaging; technical entitlements controlled via add-ons + account flags.

- Dedicated Capacity tiers:
  - Dedicated Capacity — Base (reserved capacity; standard SLA targets)
  - Dedicated Capacity — Premium (reserved capacity + premium SLA add-on included)
  Note: Specific GPU type/size is not embedded in the public SKU name to avoid churn; capacity details live in the private offer / order form and Redwood order confirmation.

- Private Deployment tiers:
  - Private Deployment — VPC (base platform license)
  - Private Deployment — Regulated (includes Compliance Pack + longer retention; language vetted by Security/GRC)

4) Add-ons structure (what is separate vs bundled)
- Separate add-ons (preferred):
  - Add-on — Compliance Pack
  - Add-on — Audit Log Retention (365 days)
  - Add-on — Premium SLA
- Bundling rules:
  - If marketplace limitations make separate add-ons hard to transact, we will provide "Premium" / "Regulated" SKUs where the add-on is included (but still represented as internal entitlements for provisioning).
  - Console must show active entitlements regardless of whether they came from a bundled SKU vs separate add-on line item.

Canonical SKU catalog (public-facing)
A) Hosted API
- "Redwood Inference — Hosted API — Starter"
- "Redwood Inference — Hosted API — Business"
- "Redwood Inference — Hosted API — Enterprise"

B) Dedicated Capacity
- "Redwood Inference — Dedicated Capacity — Base"
- "Redwood Inference — Dedicated Capacity — Premium"

C) Private Deployment
- "Redwood Inference — Private Deployment — VPC"
- "Redwood Inference — Private Deployment — Regulated"

D) Add-ons
- "Redwood Inference — Add-on — Compliance Pack"
- "Redwood Inference — Add-on — Audit Log Retention (365d)"
- "Redwood Inference — Add-on — Premium SLA"

Mapping to internal plans + entitlements (for billing/provisioning)
Notes
- Internal representation must remain stable even if marketplaces require re-issuing SKUs.
- Plan code = what Billing/Console uses for base plan.
- Entitlement IDs = feature flags / capability grants consumed by Console + control plane.

Base plans (internal)
- Hosted API
  - Public SKU: Hosted API — Starter
    - internal_plan_code: HOSTED_STARTER
    - base_entitlements: ENT_HOSTED_API
  - Public SKU: Hosted API — Business
    - internal_plan_code: HOSTED_BUSINESS
    - base_entitlements: ENT_HOSTED_API
  - Public SKU: Hosted API — Enterprise
    - internal_plan_code: HOSTED_ENTERPRISE
    - base_entitlements: ENT_HOSTED_API

- Dedicated Capacity
  - Public SKU: Dedicated Capacity — Base
    - internal_plan_code: DEDICATED_BASE
    - base_entitlements: ENT_DEDICATED_CAPACITY
  - Public SKU: Dedicated Capacity — Premium
    - internal_plan_code: DEDICATED_PREMIUM
    - base_entitlements: ENT_DEDICATED_CAPACITY, ENT_PREMIUM_SLA

- Private Deployment
  - Public SKU: Private Deployment — VPC
    - internal_plan_code: PRIVATE_VPC
    - base_entitlements: ENT_PRIVATE_CONTROL_PLANE
  - Public SKU: Private Deployment — Regulated
    - internal_plan_code: PRIVATE_REGULATED
    - base_entitlements: ENT_PRIVATE_CONTROL_PLANE, ENT_COMPLIANCE_PACK, ENT_AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_365

Add-ons (internal entitlements)
- Add-on — Compliance Pack
  - entitlement_id: ENT_COMPLIANCE_PACK
- Add-on — Audit Log Retention (365d)
  - entitlement_id: ENT_AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_365
- Add-on — Premium SLA
  - entitlement_id: ENT_PREMIUM_SLA

Console display requirements (so naming actually helps onboarding)
- Console should display:
  - Marketplace provider (AWS/GCP)
  - Purchased product family (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
  - Current internal plan (e.g., PRIVATE_VPC)
  - Active entitlements (e.g., ENT_COMPLIANCE_PACK)
  - Clear language when an entitlement is part of a bundled plan vs separate add-on purchase.
- Error messaging must avoid repeating marketplace SKU IDs; show canonical names instead.

Non-decisions / deferred items
- Exact committed spend amounts / price points are not finalized here (tracked in Finance + packaging doc); naming convention must not encode pricing.
- Upgrade/downgrade policy across marketplace purchases is tracked in PM-876 (needed copy + technical plan).
- Whether GCP requires different SKU granularity vs AWS: handled in listing implementation tickets; canonical naming stands.

Stakeholder alignment / sign-off
- PM owners: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated), Vivek Kulkarni (Private)
- Marketing/PMM: Soojin Lee (copy consistency)
- Billing: Cole Summers (plan code mapping), Nadia Rahman (metering attribution)
- Finance: Laura Bennett (marketplace fee guardrails)
- Security/GRC: Dr. Aisha Rahman + Olga Petrov reviewed that "Regulated" naming is acceptable only if we avoid overpromising; listing copy will reference specific controls rather than imply certification.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Canonical SKU taxonomy + naming convention documented and shared with PMM/Partnerships
- [x] Base plan codes + entitlement IDs defined for every canonical SKU/add-on
- [x] Mapping is unambiguous for provisioning (SKU → plan → entitlements)
- [x] Dedicated and Private SKUs avoid embedding mutable infra details (GPU type/size) in the SKU name
- [x] Add-on bundling rules are explicit (separate vs included) and compatible with Console entitlement display
